historical_patterns.broken_invariant_class: Share/accounting value cannot be moved by transient price state.
defensive_checks: Document oracle freshness, bounds, and fallback behavior.
Test deposit, withdraw, and totalAssets under mocked stale and bounded prices.
Prefer TWAP, sanity bounds, or explicit staleness checks where the design depends on external prices.
historical_patterns.failed_assumption_class: Price source remains representative during deposits, withdrawals, and share conversions.
historical_patterns.name: Harvest/Yearn-style oracle or pool price readiness gap
historical_patterns.suggested_test: Invariant: share price and totalAssets cannot be inflated by a single mocked price or pool-state movement.
historical_patterns.why_it_matters: Vault accounting that depends on oracle, pool, LP, or reserve pricing needs explicit tests for stale, spot, and manipulated local price assumptions.

historical_patterns.broken_invariant_class: Deposits, withdrawals, redemptions, and fee paths conserve value within expected rounding bounds.
defensive_checks: Add totalAssets consistency tests.
Add deposit-withdraw roundtrip tests across small and large amounts.
Test donation, zero-supply, rounding, and fee paths.
historical_patterns.failed_assumption_class: Shares and assets remain exchangeable according to documented accounting rules.
historical_patterns.name: Vault accounting invariant readiness gap
historical_patterns.suggested_test: Invariant: deposit followed by withdraw does not create value and does not strand assets beyond expected rounding.
historical_patterns.why_it_matters: Vaults need explicit conservation and roundtrip properties because share math, fees, donations, and rounding can break user-value assumptions.

historical_patterns.broken_invariant_class: Strategy lifecycle events cannot silently break totalAssets, share price, or withdrawal accounting.
defensive_checks: Test harvest/report gain and loss paths with local mocks.
Test strategy withdrawal and migration accounting.
Document trusted strategy roles and loss-handling assumptions.
historical_patterns.failed_assumption_class: Strategy-reported balances, gains, losses, and debt remain aligned with vault accounting.
historical_patterns.name: Strategy debt/gain/loss accounting readiness gap
historical_patterns.suggested_test: Invariant: strategy gain/loss reports update totalAssets and share accounting according to documented policy.
historical_patterns.why_it_matters: Strategy vaults need explicit tests for gain, loss, debt, harvest, report, and migration lifecycle assumptions.

historical_patterns.broken_invariant_class: Withdrawal lifecycle preserves shares/assets accounting and available liquidity assumptions.
defensive_checks: Test request, cancel, claim, cooldown, and epoch transitions.
Test available liquidity and buffer boundaries.
Document delayed withdrawal assumptions for auditors.
historical_patterns.failed_assumption_class: Requested, pending, claimable, and cancelled withdrawals move through documented states only.
historical_patterns.name: Withdrawal liquidity and queue lifecycle readiness gap
historical_patterns.suggested_test: Test: withdrawal lifecycle conserves shares and assets across request, cooldown, claim, and cancellation.
historical_patterns.why_it_matters: Withdrawal queues, cooldowns, epochs, and liquidity buffers need lifecycle tests because user exits depend on state transitions over time.

historical_patterns.broken_invariant_class: Emergency and configuration changes preserve the user-facing safety properties the protocol claims.
defensive_checks: Test unauthorized calls for each setter and emergency function.
Test pause and emergency controls against deposit, withdraw, redeem, and strategy paths.
Document trusted-role powers and operational limits.
historical_patterns.failed_assumption_class: Privileged operations are limited to documented roles and cannot bypass accounting assumptions silently.
historical_patterns.name: Privileged vault controls and emergency operation readiness gap
historical_patterns.suggested_test: Invariant: admin operations cannot bypass vault accounting without explicit, documented trust assumptions.
historical_patterns.why_it_matters: Vault admin operations can change strategy, oracle, fee, limits, slippage, pause state, or upgrade targets and should be tested as launch-critical boundaries.

historical_patterns.broken_invariant_class: Value flow remains single-entry and accounting is updated before control leaves the contract.
defensive_checks: Review checks-effects-interactions order.
Add reentrancy tests using local receiver mocks.
Use guards where the protocol design requires them.
historical_patterns.failed_assumption_class: External receivers cannot re-enter before internal accounting reaches a safe state.
historical_patterns.name: Reentrancy-sensitive value flow review recommended
historical_patterns.suggested_test: Test: malicious local receiver cannot withdraw, claim, or redeem twice through a callback.
historical_patterns.why_it_matters: External calls around withdrawals, claims, callbacks, or token transfers have repeatedly exposed state-ordering assumptions.

historical_patterns.broken_invariant_class: Admin actions cannot silently bypass accounting, oracle, or user-safety invariants.
defensive_checks: Document every privileged role and setter.
Add unauthorized-call tests for each privileged function.
Add tests showing pause/emergency controls behave as documented.
historical_patterns.failed_assumption_class: Privileged actors can only perform documented, intended operations.
historical_patterns.name: Privileged control and operational risk review recommended
historical_patterns.suggested_test: Invariant: unprivileged callers cannot change fees, oracles, strategies, treasury, pause state, or upgrade target.
historical_patterns.why_it_matters: Admin setters, emergency controls, fee updates, and governance execution paths can become launch blockers if role boundaries are unclear or untested.

historical_patterns.broken_invariant_class: Claimable rewards cannot exceed funded rewards beyond documented rounding.
defensive_checks: Test claim conservation across multiple users.
Test stake/unstake around reward updates.
Check precision and rounding around small balances.
historical_patterns.failed_assumption_class: Reward index math always reflects actual funded rewards and stake weights.
historical_patterns.name: Reward accounting mismatch review recommended
historical_patterns.suggested_test: Invariant: total claimed plus remaining claimable never exceeds funded rewards beyond expected rounding.
historical_patterns.why_it_matters: Reward indexes and accumulators are common sources of overclaim, underclaim, and precision drift when supply changes across epochs.

next_steps: Add Foundry invariant tests for accounting, roles, and value-flow boundaries.
Document and test oracle freshness, decimals normalization, bounds, and fallback behavior.
Add deposit/withdraw roundtrip, totalAssets consistency, and donation/inflation-resistance tests.
Add convertToShares/convertToAssets rounding tests and preview/action equivalence checks for ERC4626-like flows.
Add local mock strategy tests for gain, loss, debt, harvest, and migration accounting.

suggested_invariants.description: totalAssets should match local asset accounting and strategy balances within documented rounding.

suggested_invariants.description: A user should not create value by depositing and withdrawing through normal paths.
suggested_invariants.name: deposit/withdraw roundtrip

suggested_invariants.description: Conversion functions should be mutually consistent within documented rounding across supply states.
suggested_invariants.name: convertToShares/convertToAssets consistency

suggested_invariants.description: Donations, low supply, and external balances should not let one actor distort share value unexpectedly.
suggested_invariants.name: share price donation resistance

suggested_invariants.description: Fees should be bounded, documented, and unable to overcharge beyond configured limits.
suggested_invariants.name: fee accounting conservation

suggested_invariants.description: Strategy gains, losses, and withdrawals should remain reflected in accounting assumptions.
suggested_invariants.name: strategy balance drift handling

suggested_invariants.description: Queued or delayed withdrawals should conserve shares/assets through request, cooldown, claim, and cancellation.
suggested_invariants.name: withdrawal lifecycle conservation

suggested_invariants.description: Pause should block risky flows while preserving documented emergency exits.
suggested_invariants.name: pause behavior

suggested_invariants.description: Stale oracle rounds should be rejected or handled according to documented policy.
suggested_invariants.name: stale price rejection

suggested_invariants.description: Price decimals should be normalized consistently before accounting decisions.
suggested_invariants.name: decimals normalization

suggested_invariants.description: Outlier prices should hit documented bounds or review paths.
suggested_invariants.name: price bounds

suggested_invariants.description: Spot price dependence should be bounded by TWAP, sanity checks, or explicit assumptions.
suggested_invariants.name: TWAP or sanity check

suggested_invariants.description: Only authorized roles should change oracle configuration.
suggested_invariants.name: oracle update access control

suggested_invariants.description: Total claimed plus remaining claimable should not exceed funded rewards beyond rounding.
suggested_invariants.name: reward conservation

suggested_invariants.description: Users should not claim more than their funded and accrued share.

suggested_invariants.description: Reward indexes should be monotonic and supply-aware.
suggested_invariants.name: index monotonicity

suggested_invariants.description: Stake and unstake flows should preserve balances and reward accounting.
suggested_invariants.name: stake/unstake roundtrip

suggested_invariants.description: Small balances and precision edges should not create systematic reward drift.
suggested_invariants.name: reward accounting precision
